Theme

Nature & food

undergrowth noun

also underbrush, thicket, brambles, scrub (bushes), brushwood, thorn bush, copse, scrub, bushes, brier

classical

Cic. Tusc. 5.64
Verg. G. 1.15 (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 400

dūmētum, dūmētī n.

noun, second declension

a thicket, thorny undergrowth; often plural, dūmēta

Other words

  • vepris, vepris m. — a thorn-bush, bramble (usually plural, veprēs)

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Tusc. 5.64

  • dūmus, dūmī m. — a thorn bush, a bramble

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Cic. Tusc. 5.65 (Lewis & Short); Verg. G. 3.315 (Lewis & Short)

  • sentis, sentis m. — a thorn bush, a brier (usually plural, sentēs)

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Caes. BG 2.17 (Lewis & Short); Verg. E. 4.29 (Lewis & Short); Lucr. 5.207 (Lewis & Short)

    Mostly in the poets, not in Cicero. Sentis canis is Columella’s name for the dog rose (11.3.4, Lewis & Short).

  • virgulta, virgultōrum n. pl. — bushes, brushwood, a thicket

    noun, second declension, plural · also used · classical · Caes. BG 3.18 (Lewis & Short); Liv. 1.14.7 (Lewis & Short); Cic. Cael. 42 (Lewis & Short)

  • fruticētum, fruticētī n. — a thicket, a place full of bushes

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Hor. C. 3.12.12 (Lewis & Short); Suet. Ner. 48 (Lewis & Short)

  • spīnētum, spīnētī n. — a thicket of thorns

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Verg. E. 2.9 (Lewis & Short); Plin. NH 10.204 (Lewis & Short)

Examples

  • saeptum undique et vestītum vepribus et dūmētīs indāgāvī sepulcrum

    I tracked down the tomb, hedged all round and clothed in brambles and thicketsCic. Tusc. 5.64

  • incultīsque rubēns pendēbit sentibus ūva

    and the reddening grape will hang from wild briersVerg. E. 4.29

  • dum tenera attondent sīmae virgulta capellae

    while the snub-nosed goats crop the tender bushesVerg. E. 10.7

  • nunc viridēs etiam occultant spīnēta lacertōs

    now even the thorn thickets hide the green lizardsVerg. E. 2.9

See also bramble, forest, bush, thorn, fern, thorn bush.
